normalization.title: A benchmark is not a lab: what one AI-biology trial actually measured
normalization.overview: Active Site's physical-lab trial tests whether mid-2025 frontier AI helped novices complete a defined three-task sequence, while separate studies probe different outcomes.
normalization.whyItMatters: For safety evaluators and model builders, the key distinction is digital ability, partial human progress, and completed physical work; this trial cannot forecast current models.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Record actor, model date, access, comparator, task, final outcome, intermediate progress, and safeguards before drawing a risk or safety conclusion; repeat matched human-outcome tests when those conditions change.
normalization.falsification: A larger, independently run physical-lab study with a specified newer system and pre-registered consequential human outcomes would change the uplift estimate for that setting.
normalization.freshness: Active Site and METR are the same trial family; LANL is a separate, small physical task; AISI reports different digital measures. No interview speech is used.

claims.proposition: Active Site randomized 153 novices, 76 internet and 77 AI, across 39 four-hour sessions in June-August 2025.
claims.assessment: Direct original study report; preprint, not independent replication. Most participants were undergraduates.
claims.limits: Direct original study report; preprint, not independent replication. Most participants were undergraduates.

claims.proposition: Intervention offered mid-2025 benchmark-selected frontier models from three vendors without safety classifiers.
claims.assessment: Direct design fact. Does not describe normal consumer safeguards or 2026 models.
claims.limits: Direct design fact. Does not describe normal consumer safeguards or 2026 models.

claims.proposition: Primary endpoint was success on a three-core-task sequence, 4/77 versus 5/76, RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.24-2.62, P = 0.759.
claims.assessment: Pre-registered primary outcome; no significant difference detected. It was not a fully integrated real-world project.
claims.limits: Pre-registered primary outcome; no significant difference detected. It was not a fully integrated real-world project.

claims.proposition: Four of five individual tasks numerically favored AI; no full-cohort individual-task success result was significant.
claims.assessment: Secondary measures. Do not report direction alone as proof of uplift.
claims.limits: Secondary measures. Do not report direction alone as proof of uplift.

claims.proposition: Cell-culture success was 68.8% versus 55.3% in the full cohort (P = 0.059), and 79.7% versus 62.5% among 128 per-protocol participants (P = 0.025).
claims.assessment: Different analysis sets; the latter is a subset result, not the primary endpoint.
claims.limits: Different analysis sets; the latter is a subset result, not the primary endpoint.

claims.proposition: Post-hoc modeled typical-task RR was 1.42 (95% credible interval 0.74-2.62); progress measures favored AI at many intermediate steps.
claims.assessment: Exploratory/model-dependent and intermediate outcomes; cannot become final physical completion.
claims.limits: Exploratory/model-dependent and intermediate outcomes; cannot become final physical completion.

claims.proposition: The study excluded acquisition and lab setup and split the task sequence; low completion reduced power to 36% for OR 2 and 73% for OR 3 in post-hoc calculations.
claims.assessment: Investigator-reported limits. Do not convert absence of significance into absence of risk.
claims.limits: Investigator-reported limits. Do not convert absence of significance into absence of risk.

claims.proposition: In an independent ten-person physical-lab pilot, the authors report 3/5 AI versus 1/5 internet completed on the first attempt, and 4/5 versus 3/5 after two attempts.
claims.assessment: Different task/model and limited expert help; tiny descriptive study, no precise uplift estimate or replication of P03. The narrative says only one additional internet participant completed on retry, inconsistent with its reported 3/5 final total. Its HTML body bears an inconsistent later date, so the arXiv submission history anchors the version date.
claims.limits: Different task/model and limited expert help; tiny descriptive study, no precise uplift estimate or replication of P03. The narrative says only one additional internet participant completed on retry, inconsistent with its reported 3/5 final total. Its HTML body bears an inconsistent later date, so the arXiv submission history anchors the version date.

claims.proposition: AISI reports stronger biology knowledge/protocol/troubleshooting evaluations and an unquantified internal novice-lab success signal.
claims.assessment: Independent public capability signal. Some protocol feasibility checks occurred, but no published matched novice/control result establishes uplift or validates P03.
claims.limits: Independent public capability signal. Some protocol feasibility checks occurred, but no published matched novice/control result establishes uplift or validates P03.

claims.proposition: Interviewed practitioners identify shifting models, baselines, and user skill as threats to uplift-study generalization.
claims.assessment: Methodology evidence from 16 expert interviews; includes Active Site author overlap, so not an independent outcome replication.
claims.limits: Methodology evidence from 16 expert interviews; includes Active Site author overlap, so not an independent outcome replication.

claims.proposition: A METR collaborator reports the Active Site trial cost $1.9 million and took four dedicated staff more than a year.
claims.assessment: Participant account of effort, not audited cost data or an independent replication. Supports a cadence argument only.
claims.limits: Participant account of effort, not audited cost data or an independent replication. Supports a cadence argument only.

claims.proposition: Gates publicly warns that AI could magnify biological misuse.
claims.assessment: Same-speaker editorial context only. No claim about what Gates said in the held interview or proof of physical uplift.
claims.limits: Same-speaker editorial context only. No claim about what Gates said in the held interview or proof of physical uplift.

claims.proposition: Model answer, assisted human progress, and completed physical work require distinct evidence.
claims.assessment: Original editorial interpretation, not a reported study endpoint. Revise if a newer matched human-outcome study changes the relationship.
claims.limits: Original editorial interpretation, not a reported study endpoint. Revise if a newer matched human-outcome study changes the relationship.
